tools.name: list-connections
tools.title: List Connections
tools.description: List all saved TablePro database connections with their id, name, type (postgresql, mysql, sqlite, etc.), host, and port. Call this first when the user names a connection so you can pass its id to other tools. Returns an empty list when no connections are saved; throws when the user has not paired the extension with TablePro.

tools.name: list-databases
tools.title: List Databases
tools.description: List database names on a TablePro connection. Use for engines that group objects under a database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MS SQL, ClickHouse). Skip for SQLite, Redis, MongoDB.

tools.name: list-schemas
tools.title: List Schemas
tools.description: List schema names in a database. Use for engines that have schemas inside a database (PostgreSQL, MS SQL, Oracle, Redshift). Pass the database for engines that need it; omit for engines that do not separate database and schema.

tools.name: list-tables
tools.title: List Tables
tools.description: List tables in a connection, optionally scoped to a database or schema. Returns name, schema, database, type (table or view), and approximate row count. Call describe-table next when you need column types.

tools.name: describe-table
tools.title: Describe Table
tools.description: Return the column list, data types, nullability, primary-key flags, defaults, and comments for a table. Always call this before generating queries against a table you have not seen so the SQL matches the real schema.

tools.name: get-table-ddl
tools.title: Get Table DDL
tools.description: Return the CREATE TABLE statement for a table, including indexes and constraints when the engine supports it. Use this when the user asks how a table is defined or wants to copy the structure.

tools.name: run-query
tools.title: Run Query
tools.description: Execute a SQL query against a connection and return columns and rows. Mutating SQL (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, MERGE, CREATE) goes through user confirmation; never bypass it. Result rows are capped at 200 by default; pass rowLimit to lower that. The connection's external-access setting can reject the query as read-only; surface that error to the user verbatim.

tools.name: explain-query
tools.title: Explain Query
tools.description: Wrap a query with EXPLAIN and return the execution plan. Use when the user asks why a query is slow or how the database will run it. Does not run the underlying query.

tools.name: open-connection-window
tools.title: Open Connection in TablePro
tools.description: Open the TablePro window for a connection so the user can continue interactively. Prefer this over streaming large result sets in chat when the user wants to inspect, edit, or filter data.

tools.name: search-history
tools.title: Search Query History
tools.description: Full-text search the saved TablePro query history. Returns query text, connection id, executed-at timestamp, duration, and row count. Use to find prior work the user is referencing.

ai.instructions: TablePro is a native macOS database client. Use list-connections first to resolve the user's description to a connection id, then pass that id to other tools. Always describe-table before generating SQL against a table you have not seen. For mutating SQL (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, MERGE) the run-query tool routes through user confirmation; never bypass that and never tell the user a mutation ran without confirming the tool returned successfully. The connection's external-access setting may reject your query as read-only; surface that error verbatim. Prefer open-connection-window when the user wants to inspect or edit data interactively rather than streaming rows in chat. If a tool throws TokenMissingError or TableProNotInstalledError, tell the user to run the Pair with TablePro Raycast command (or install TablePro from tablepro.app) and stop calling tools until they do; do not retry.
